A huge boiler that grows with its size. Count its sections: width × depth ÷ 9 × height (a 3×3×3 is 3, the largest, a 7×7×16, is 87.1). Per section it holds 100,000 HU and 16,000 mB of water and steam. It boils with up to the largest's 50,400 HU/t shared by its sections, about 579 HU/t each: a 3×3×3 boils with up to 1,736 HU/t. Each mB costs 8 HU of Steam, 12 of High-Pressure or 16 of Superheated.
Build a hollow box: a footprint 3 to 7 by 3 to 7 (it needn't be square), 3 to 16 tall. In a 3×3 tower only the corners must be casings; in a bigger one all twelve edges must be. Anywhere else can be Pressure Glass, so you can watch the water and steam inside.
Keep other loose casings and glass from touching it while you build, or it forms only as a 3×3.
# Pressure
Its Pressure tab picks the grade. On Auto it boils all the heat above 100°C: feed it more heat than it boils and it climbs toward its heat source's temperature, making better steam; underfeed it and it holds at 100°C making plain Steam.
Set to Steam, High-Pressure or Superheated, it heats without boiling until it reaches that grade's temperature, then holds there, making that grade at whatever rate its heat comes in.
If it cools into a lower grade, the steam it holds drops to that grade.
